text:
Because the nature of emptiness is non-existent, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the final limit. Because the essence of non-existence is the emptiness of emptiness, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the final limit. Because the essence of non-existence is the emptiness of seclusion, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the final limit. Because the non-existence of things is the non-existence of the essence of emptiness, and because the essence of existing emptiness is the non-existence of essence, the Bodhisattva is not perceived at the final limit. Because the essence of non-existence is the non-existence of emptiness, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle.

The essence of non-existence is emptiness. Because the essence of non-existence is the emptiness of seclusion, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. The Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. The Bodhisattva is not perceived in the three <note>referring to the three times: past, present, and future</note>. The Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. Because the essence of non-existence is the emptiness of emptiness, the Bodhisattva is not perceived in the middle. Why is this? Venerable son of Sharadvati <note>a name for Shariputra, a primary disciple of the Buddha</note>, the non-existence of the essence of emptiness, the emptiness of the essence of non-existence, the seclusion of the essence of non-existence, and the non-existence of the essence of the emptiness of non-existence do not perceive a past limit.

<summary>This text discusses the philosophical concept of emptiness (shunyata) and the non-perception of the Bodhisattva across the limits of time and space.</summary>
<keywords>Bodhisattva, emptiness, shunyata, Shariputra, non-existence, essence</keywords>
